full_judgment: The opposite party, Mr. Arif Ahmed as a plaintiff filed SCC Suit No. 10 of 1985 in the 3rd Court of Assistant Judge and SCC Judge, Camilla for eviction of the defendant Mr. Faiz Ahmed Chowdhury from the suit premises. The case of the plaintiff is that the suit land originally belonged to Maharaja of Tripura who subsequently made a settlement of the same to Nibaran Chandra Ganguli by a registered patta dated 23-9-1938 and that Nibaran Chandra Ganguli constructed a building in the suit property after taking settlement from the Maharaja of Tripura. Thereafter, Nibaran Chandradied leaving behind 4 sons, namely, Mukunda Chandra Ganguli, Nirrnal Chandra Ganguli, Nipendra Chandra Ganguli and Nirode Ganguli and on amicable arrangement Mukunda Chandra became the owner of the other property and the other three brothers became owners of the suit property. The 3 brothers subsequently exchanged their property with one Abdus Sattar and others by way of general power of attorney executed on 17-4-64 which was regularised by way of a registered deed of exchange dated 1-8-67. Abdus Sattar and others again made an exchange of the same property with the plaintiff by a registered deed dated 29-12-80. The defendant who was a tenant under Abdus Sattar in the suit premises became tenat under the plaintiff firstly at a monthly rent of Taka 10.00, then at the rate of Taka 30.00 and finally at the rate of Taka 40.00 per month. But the defendant defaulted in payment of rent and that the plaintiff also required the suit premises for his own bonafide use and occupation and as such, the plaintiff terminated the tenancy of the defendant by serving a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act and then filed the SCC Suit as aforesaid.
